0.title: One God in Three Persons
0.overview:
Christians believe in one God who exists eternally as three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Each is fully God, yet there are not three gods but one. This is the doctrine of the Trinity. The word "Trinity" is not found in the Bible, but the truth it names is found on almost every page of the New Testament.

Many believers find the Trinity confusing and quietly avoid it. Some think of it as a puzzle for theologians with little to do with everyday faith. Yet the Trinity is not a footnote to Christianity. It is the shape of the God we worship. Every Christian prayer is offered to the Father, through the Son, by the Spirit. Every Christian is baptised in the one name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit (Matt 28:19). Salvation itself is the work of the three persons together.

We will never fully comprehend the Trinity; we are creatures speaking of our Creator. But we can know what Scripture says, avoid the errors that distort it and grow in love for the God who has revealed himself as Father, Son and Spirit.

Six units: (1) One God; (2) Three Persons; (3) The Trinity Revealed; (4) Guarding the Truth; (5) The Trinity and Our Salvation; (6) Living with the Triune God. This study belongs with the Attributes of God and the studies on Christ and the Holy Spirit.

1.title: One God
1.overview:
The foundation of the doctrine of the Trinity is that there is only one God. Christianity is not polytheism.

Israel's confession. Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one (Deut 6:4). Israel was to speak these words when lying down and when rising up (Deut 6:7). In a world crowded with gods, Israel worshipped one. I am the LORD, and there is no other, besides me there is no God (Isa 45:5).

The New Testament agrees. Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:4 as the beginning of the greatest commandment (Mark 12:29). Paul wrote, we know that "an idol has no real existence," and that "there is no God but one." (1 Cor 8:4). James says, You believe that God is one; you do well (Jas 2:19). The first Christians were Jews who never stopped believing in one God.

One God, not a committee. The Father, Son and Spirit are not three gods working together like partners in a business. They share one divine being, one will and one power. Whatever God does, the three persons do together.

Why this matters. If there were many gods, the world would have no single source, no single standard of truth and no single object of worship. The oneness of God means that all of life belongs to him, and that he alone deserves our whole heart. That is why the Shema is followed immediately by the command: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might (Deut 6:5).
1.theology:
Unity of being: When Christians say God is one, they mean that there is one divine nature or being. The three persons do not each have a third of God. Each is the whole God. This is a mystery beyond our full understanding, but it is not a contradiction: God is one in one sense (being) and three in another (persons).

Monotheism and the Trinity: Some, such as Muslims and Jehovah's Witnesses, claim that the Trinity is a form of belief in three gods. Christians reply that the doctrine of the Trinity is the safeguard of monotheism, not its denial, because it insists that the Son and Spirit share the one being of God rather than being lesser gods beside him.

No rivals: Because God is one, there is no rival power equal to him. Satan is a creature, not an evil god.
1.examples:
Then: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. They cried out all day, and no one answered. Elijah prayed once, and fire fell. The people shouted, The LORD, he is God; the LORD, he is God (1 Kgs 18:39). There is one God, and he answers.

Now: A Christian is talking with a Muslim colleague who says Christians believe in three gods. She explains that Christians recite the same confession as Moses: the LORD is one. Then she opens the Gospel of John and shows how Jesus spoke of the Father, himself and the Spirit. They agree to keep talking.

A simple test: If someone asked you whether Christians believe in three gods, how would you answer?

verseByVerse.quote: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Shema is the heart of Israel's faith. The LORD is one, so he must be loved with the whole person. There is no room for a divided heart, because there is no other god to share it with. Christians still confess these words, now knowing the one God as Father, Son and Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: I am the LORD, and there is no other, besides me there is no God; I equip you, though you do not know me, that people may know, from the rising of the sun and from the west, that there is none besides me; I am the LORD, and there is no other. I form light and create darkness; I make well-being and create calamity; I am the LORD, who does all these things. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God speaks to Cyrus, a pagan king he will use to free his people. There is no other God. He forms light and creates darkness; he makes well-being and creates calamity. Everything comes from the one LORD, so that people from east to west may know there is none besides him.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, as to the eating of food offered to idols, we know that "an idol has no real existence," and that "there is no God but one." For although there may be so-called gods in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many "gods" and many "lords"— yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul writes about food offered to idols. Idols are nothing, because there is one God. Then he says something remarkable: there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ. He places Jesus inside the confession of the one God, using the word "Lord" from the Shema. The one God is Father and Son.

verseByVerse.quote: And one of the scribes came up and heard them disputing with one another, and seeing that he answered them well, asked him, "Which commandment is the most important of all?" Jesus answered, "The most important is, 'Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.' (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: A scribe asked which commandment is most important. Jesus answered with the Shema. The Son of God himself confesses that the Lord is one. There is no tension between the oneness of God and the deity of Christ; Jesus held both.

1.reflection:
Why is it important that Christians believe in one God, not three?

How does 1 Corinthians 8:6 include Jesus in the confession of the one God?

What does the oneness of God mean for how we love him?

How would you explain to a friend that the Trinity is not belief in three gods?

2.title: Three Persons
2.overview:
Alongside the oneness of God, the New Testament shows that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are each fully God, and that they are distinct from one another.

The Father is God. This is everywhere assumed. Jesus prays to the only true God as Father (John 17:3). Paul begins his letters with grace from God our Father (Rom 1:7).

The Son is God. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God (John 1:1). Thomas confessed, My Lord and my God! (John 20:28). Paul says that in Christ the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily (Col 2:9). The Father himself says of the Son, Your throne, O God, is forever and ever (Heb 1:8). The Son creates, forgives, receives worship and will judge, all things only God can do.

The Spirit is God. Lying to the Holy Spirit is lying to God (Acts 5:3-4). The Spirit knows the depths of God (1 Cor 2:10-11), is present everywhere (Ps 139:7) and gives life. And he is a person: he teaches, speaks, intercedes and can be grieved.

The persons are distinct. The Father is not the Son, the Son is not the Spirit, and the Spirit is not the Father. The Son prays to the Father (John 17). The Father sends the Son (John 3:17). The Son sends the Spirit from the Father (John 15:26). The Spirit speaks not on his own authority but declares what is the Son's (John 16:13-14). These are real relationships between real persons, not one person wearing three masks.

One name. Jesus told his disciples to baptise in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matt 28:19). Notice: one name, not three names. One God, three persons.
2.theology:
What "person" means: In this doctrine, a "person" is not a separate being, as three human persons are three separate beings. It means a distinct "who" within the one divine "what." Our language strains here, because nothing in creation is exactly like God.

Eternal relations: The persons are distinguished by their relations. The Father is eternally Father, never without the Son. The Son is eternally begotten of the Father, not made and not created. The Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father and the Son. These relations did not begin at creation or at Bethlehem; they are who God eternally is.

Equal in glory: The three persons are equal in power, glory and majesty. The Son is not a lesser God, nor the Spirit a divine force. Each is to be worshipped.
2.examples:
Then: In the upper room, Jesus spoke of all three persons at once: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things (John 14:26). The Father sends; the Spirit comes in the Son's name; the Spirit teaches. Three persons, one saving purpose.

Now: A Christian has always prayed to "God" without much thought about who he is addressing. Studying the Trinity, he begins to pray to the Father as a child, to give thanks for the Son by name and to ask for the Spirit's help. His prayers become warmer and richer.

A simple test: When you pray, do you think of God as Father, Son and Spirit, or as a vague single presence?

verseByVerse.quote: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him was not any thing made that was made. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Word was with God, so he is distinct from the Father. The Word was God, so he shares the Father's nature. And all things were made through him, so he is not part of creation. In three short verses John lays the foundation of the doctrine of the Trinity.

verseByVerse.quote: But of the Son he says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions." And, "You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands; they will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment, like a robe you will roll them up, like a garment they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will have no end." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The writer quotes Psalm 45 and Psalm 102 and applies both to the Son. God calls the Son God, and says he laid the foundation of the earth and will remain when heaven and earth wear out like a garment. The Son is eternal, unchanging Creator, and the Father himself says so.

verseByVerse.quote: "But when the Helper comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: In one sentence Jesus names all three persons. He will send the Helper from the Father; the Spirit proceeds from the Father; and the Spirit will bear witness about Jesus. The three are distinct, yet they act together in perfect harmony.

verseByVerse.quote: And Jesus came and said to them, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The risen Christ, with all authority, sends his disciples to baptise in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Baptism places believers under the name of the Triune God. From the first day of the Christian life, the Trinity is the God we belong to.

2.reflection:
Which verses most clearly show you that the Son is fully God? That the Spirit is fully God?

How does Scripture show that the Father, Son and Spirit are distinct persons?

What does it mean to be baptised into the "name" of the Father, Son and Spirit?

How could thinking of God as three persons enrich your prayers?

3.title: The Trinity Revealed
3.overview:
The doctrine of the Trinity was not invented by philosophers. It was revealed gradually by God, in history, and finally in the coming of the Son and the Spirit.

Hints in the Old Testament. The Old Testament emphasises God's oneness, but it contains hints of plurality within God. Let us make man in our image (Gen 1:26). The Spirit of God hovers over the waters at creation (Gen 1:2). The angel of the LORD speaks as God and is called God (Gen 16:13; Exod 3:2-6). God's Word and Wisdom act as if personal (Ps 33:6; Prov 8). The Messiah is called Mighty God, Everlasting Father (Isa 9:6). And in Isaiah, the Servant says, And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit (Isa 48:16). Read in the light of Christ, these hints become clearer.

Revealed in the Gospels. The full revelation came with Jesus. At his baptism, all three persons appeared together. And when Jesus was baptized, immediately he went up from the water, and behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming to rest on him; and behold, a voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased." (Matt 3:16-17). The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, the Father speaks.

Revealed in Jesus' teaching. Jesus spoke constantly of his Father and promised the Spirit. In John 14-17, the night before his death, he spoke of the three persons more than anywhere else. The Father loves the Son, the Son obeys the Father, the Spirit glorifies the Son.

Revealed in the apostles' worship. The early church did not sit down and design a doctrine. They worshipped Jesus as Lord, experienced the Spirit poured out and prayed to the Father. Their letters are full of Trinitarian patterns, often without any explanation, because this was simply how they knew God (1 Pet 1:2; Jude 20-21).
3.theology:
Revelation in action: God revealed the Trinity not mainly by explaining it, but by acting: the Father sending the Son, the Son dying and rising, the Spirit being poured out. We know who God is by what he has done to save us.

The Old Testament read rightly: We should not claim that Old Testament believers fully understood the Trinity. But the New Testament shows that the same God was at work all along, and invites us to reread the Old Testament with new eyes (Luke 24:27).

"Let us": Some explain Genesis 1:26 as God speaking to angels, or as a plural of majesty. But angels did not create humanity, and the image is God's alone. In the light of the New Testament, many Christians have seen here a hint of the Trinity.
3.examples:
Then: At Pentecost, Peter explained what had happened: Jesus, being therefore exalted at the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this that you yourselves are seeing and hearing (Acts 2:33). Peter's first sermon was Trinitarian without using the word.

Now: A Bible study group reading Genesis 1 discusses the words "Let us make man." One member, new to the faith, says, "So the Trinity was there from the beginning?" The leader turns to John 1:1-3 and Genesis 1:2. The group sees the Father, the Word and the Spirit together at creation.

A simple test: Next time you read a Gospel, look for places where the Father, Son and Spirit appear together.

verseByVerse.quote: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was without form and void, and darkness was over the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters. And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God creates the heavens and the earth. The Spirit of God hovers over the waters. God speaks, and light appears. John later tells us that the Word through whom God spoke is the Son (John 1:1-3). At creation, the one God acts as Father, Word and Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him. John would have prevented him, saying, "I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?" But Jesus answered him, "Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he consented. And when Jesus was baptized, immediately he went up from the water, and behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming to rest on him; and behold, a voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John hesitated to baptise Jesus, but Jesus insisted, to fulfil all righteousness. Then the heavens opened. The Spirit descended like a dove; the Father declared his love for his Son. Here the three persons are revealed together at the start of Jesus' public ministry.

verseByVerse.quote: Draw near to me, hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret, from the time it came to be I have been there." And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: In the middle of God's speech in Isaiah, a voice says, the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit. The one sent speaks as if he has been with God from the beginning. Read in the light of the New Testament, this hints at the Father sending the Son with the Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, To those who are elect exiles of the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and for sprinkling with his blood: May grace and peace be multiplied to you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter's greeting is packed with the Trinity: chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and for sprinkling with his blood. Salvation is the work of all three persons, and Peter mentions them without any explanation.

3.reflection:
Which Old Testament hints of the Trinity do you find most striking?

Read Matthew 3:13-17. What does each person of the Trinity do?

Why did God reveal the Trinity gradually rather than all at once?

Look for a Trinitarian pattern in one of Paul's letters this week.

4.title: Guarding the Truth
4.overview:
Through history, many have tried to make the Trinity simpler by giving up part of what Scripture says. The church has had to guard the truth by naming these errors. Knowing them helps us avoid them today.

One person in three modes. Some taught that God is one person who appears in three ways or roles: as Father in creation, as Son in redemption and as Spirit in the church. This is called modalism. It is still common, often through illustrations like water being ice, liquid and steam. But Scripture shows the three persons existing at the same time and relating to one another. At Jesus' baptism, the Son is in the water, the Spirit descends and the Father speaks. The Son prays to the Father. Modalism turns these into a kind of play-acting.

The Son as a created being. Others taught that the Son is the first and highest creature, but not fully God. This was the teaching of Arius in the fourth century, and Jehovah's Witnesses teach it today. But Scripture says all things were made through the Son (John 1:3). He cannot be part of creation if he made all of it. He is the radiance of the glory of God and the exact imprint of his nature (Heb 1:3). The church's great creed of the fourth century confessed that the Son is true God from true God, of the same being as the Father.

Three gods. Others go the opposite way, treating the Father, Son and Spirit as three separate gods who agree with one another. This is tritheism. It denies the oneness of God that Scripture insists on.

Illustrations. Every illustration of the Trinity fails somewhere. An egg (shell, white, yolk) makes each person a part of God. Water (ice, liquid, steam) suggests modalism. A man who is a father, son and husband is one person in three roles. It is wiser to say that God is unique, and to stay with the words of Scripture.
4.theology:
"Firstborn of all creation": Jehovah's Witnesses appeal to Colossians 1:15 to say Jesus was created. But the next verse says by him all things were created (Col 1:16). "Firstborn" here means supreme rank and heir, as Israel was God's firstborn (Exod 4:22) and David was made the firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth (Ps 89:27).

"The Father is greater than I": Jesus said this (John 14:28) as the incarnate Son, in his humble role as servant. It speaks of his position in his earthly mission, not of a lesser divine nature. The same Jesus said, I and the Father are one (John 10:30).

Why the creeds matter: The early creeds did not add to Scripture. They summarised it and fenced it against error. Believers today stand with the church through the ages when they confess the Trinity.
4.examples:
Then: When Jesus said I and the Father are one, the Jews picked up stones, saying, you, being a man, make yourself God (John 10:30-33). They understood him clearly. Jesus did not correct them by saying he was a lesser being.

Now: A youth leader has always explained the Trinity using the water illustration. After learning about modalism, he changes his approach. He tells his group, "God is unlike anything else. Let's look at what the Bible says about the Father, the Son and the Spirit." The young people find the Bible's own words more convincing than the illustration.

A simple test: Which illustration of the Trinity have you used? What does it get wrong?

verseByVerse.quote: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father's hand. I and the Father are one." The Jews picked up stones again to stone him. Jesus answered them, "I have shown you many good works from the Father; for which of them are you going to stone me?" The Jews answered him, "It is not for a good work that we are going to stone you but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus says that no one can snatch his sheep out of his hand, and no one can snatch them out of the Father's hand. Then he says, I and the Father are one. They are one in power to protect, and one in being. His hearers understood it as a claim to be God, and tried to stone him for it.

verseByVerse.quote: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through him and for him. And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together. And he is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in everything he might be preeminent. For in him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, making peace by the blood of his cross. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul's hymn exalts the Son as the image of the invisible God and the firstborn over creation, by whom and for whom all things were created. He is before all things, and in him all things hold together. All the fullness of God was pleased to dwell in him. The Son is Creator, not creature.

verseByVerse.quote: Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed the heir of all things, through whom also he created the world. He is the radiance of the glory of God and the exact imprint of his nature, and he upholds the universe by the word of his power. After making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high, having become as much superior to angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Son is the heir of all things, the one through whom God created the world, the radiance of God's glory and the exact imprint of his nature. He upholds the universe. He is not an angel or a high creature; he is superior to the angels. These verses answer every attempt to make him less than God.

verseByVerse.quote: When Jesus had spoken these words, he lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, "Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son that the Son may glorify you, since you have given him authority over all flesh, to give eternal life to all whom you have given him. And this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. I glorified you on earth, having accomplished the work that you gave me to do. And now, Father, glorify me in your own presence with the glory that I had with you before the world existed. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus prays to the Father, showing that they are distinct persons. He asks to be glorified with the glory he had with the Father before the world existed. The Son is not a mode of the Father, and he is not a creature who came later. He shared the Father's glory from eternity.

4.reflection:
What is modalism, and why is it wrong?

How would you answer someone who says Colossians 1:15 shows Jesus was created?

Why do all illustrations of the Trinity fail?

Why do you think the early church thought it so important to guard the doctrine of the Trinity?

5.title: The Trinity and Our Salvation
5.overview:
The Trinity is not only a truth about God in himself. It is the shape of our salvation. Every part of it is the work of the Father, the Son and the Spirit together.

The Father plans. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places, even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world (Eph 1:3-4). Salvation begins in the Father's eternal love and choice.

The Son accomplishes. In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses (Eph 1:7). The Son became man, lived, died and rose to secure our salvation.

The Spirit applies. In him you also, when you heard the word of truth... were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit (Eph 1:13). The Spirit gives new birth, unites us to Christ and guarantees our inheritance.

Adopted into the family. Paul describes the whole Trinity at work in our adoption: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons. And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, "Abba! Father!" (Gal 4:4-6). The Father sends the Son to redeem us, and sends the Spirit to make us cry "Father."

Access to the Father. For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father (Eph 2:18). Christian prayer and worship are Trinitarian: through the Son, by the Spirit, to the Father.
5.theology:
The persons work inseparably: In every act of God, all three persons act together. Yet each act is especially associated with one person: creation with the Father, redemption with the Son, sanctification with the Spirit. We should never imagine a kind Son persuading a reluctant Father, or a Spirit acting independently of Christ.

Love before the world: Salvation flows from the eternal love of the Father for the Son in the Spirit. Jesus prays that his people may know that you sent me and loved them even as you loved me (John 17:23). We are brought into a love that existed before creation.

Union with Christ: The Spirit unites us to the Son, and in the Son we share his relationship with the Father. This is why believers can call God "Father."
5.examples:
Then: Paul's prayer for the Ephesians is Trinitarian. He bows before the Father, asks that they be strengthened by his Spirit, so that Christ may dwell in their hearts, and that they may know the love of Christ (Eph 3:14-19).

Now: A believer struggling with assurance feels that God is distant. A pastor walks her through Ephesians 1, showing how the Father chose her, the Son redeemed her and the Spirit sealed her. Her salvation does not rest on her feelings, but on the work of all three persons. She weeps with relief.

A simple test: Can you explain your salvation in terms of what the Father, the Son and the Spirit have each done?

verseByVerse.quote: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places, even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him. In love he predestined us for adoption to himself as sons through Jesus Christ, according to the purpose of his will, to the praise of his glorious grace, with which he has blessed us in the Beloved. In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace, which he lavished upon us, in all wisdom and insight making known to us the mystery of his will, according to his purpose, which he set forth in Christ as a plan for the fullness of time, to unite all things in Christ, things in heaven and things on earth in him. In him we have obtained an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will, so that we who were the first to hope in Christ might be to the praise of his glory. In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance until we acquire possession of it, to the praise of his glory. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This long sentence in Paul's original is a hymn of praise to the Triune God. The Father chose and predestined us (vv. 3-6). The Son redeemed us by his blood (vv. 7-12). The Spirit sealed us as a guarantee (vv. 13-14). Each section ends with praise to God's glory. Salvation is the Trinity's work from beginning to end.

verseByVerse.quote: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons. And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, "Abba! Father!" So you are no longer a slave, but a son, and if a son, then an heir through God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Father sent the Son at the right time to redeem slaves. Then he sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts. The result: we are no longer slaves but sons, and heirs. Adoption is a gift of the whole Trinity, and it changes how we relate to God.

verseByVerse.quote: And he came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near. For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone, in whom the whole structure, being joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord. In him you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Christ preached peace to those far and near. Through him both Jews and Gentiles have access in one Spirit to the Father. Then Paul describes the church as a temple, built on Christ, where God dwells by the Spirit. The church is the dwelling place of the Triune God.

verseByVerse.quote: "I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me. The glory that you have given me I have given to them, that they may be one even as we are one, I in them and you in me, that they may become perfectly one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them even as you loved me. Father, I desire that they also, whom you have given me, may be with me where I am, to see my glory that you have given me because you loved me before the foundation of the world. O righteous Father, even though the world does not know you, I know you, and these know that you have sent me. I made known to them your name, and I will continue to make it known, that the love with which you have loved me may be in them, and I in them." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus prays that his people will be one, as he and the Father are one. He prays that they will be with him to see his glory, given in love before the foundation of the world. And he prays that the Father's love for him will be in them. Salvation brings us into the eternal love of the Trinity.

5.reflection:
Read Ephesians 1:3-14. What does each person of the Trinity do in your salvation?

How does Galatians 4:4-7 describe the Trinity at work in our adoption?

What does it mean to have "access in one Spirit to the Father" through Christ?

How does knowing the Trinity strengthen your assurance?

6.title: Living with the Triune God
6.overview:
The Trinity is not only to be believed. It is to be lived. The God who is Father, Son and Spirit shapes our prayer, worship, relationships and hope.

Prayer. Jesus taught us to pray, Our Father in heaven (Matt 6:9). We pray in Jesus' name, trusting in his work (John 14:13). And the Spirit helps us pray, interceding for us when we do not know what to pray (Rom 8:26). Every Christian prayer is a small participation in the life of the Trinity.

Worship. Christian worship is Trinitarian. We sing to the Father, praise the Son and pray for the Spirit. Many of the church's greatest hymns and doxologies give glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit together.

Love. God is love (1 John 4:8). This is true because God has always been a fellowship of love. Before creation, the Father loved the Son (John 17:24). God did not need to create in order to have someone to love. Our love for one another reflects the love within God.

Unity in the church. Jesus prayed that his people would be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you (John 17:21). The unity of the church is meant to reflect the unity of the Trinity: many members, one body, diverse gifts, one Spirit (1 Cor 12:4-6).

The blessing. Paul ended a letter with words that churches still use: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all (2 Cor 13:14). The Triune God is not a doctrine we keep at a distance. He is the God who blesses us.

Eternity. In the new creation, we will see the glory of God in the face of Christ, filled with the Spirit, forever. The Trinity will be our eternal joy.
6.theology:
Mystery and worship: The doctrine of the Trinity should lead us not to frustration but to worship. A God we could fully understand would not be God. Paul ends his deepest theology with doxology (Rom 11:33-36).

Relationships: The Trinity shows that relationship is not an afterthought in reality. Persons in loving relationship are at the heart of all that is. This is why loneliness feels so wrong, and why community is so important for human beings made in God's image.

Balance: Healthy Christian faith honours all three persons. Some traditions neglect the Spirit; others neglect the Father or focus only on the Spirit's gifts. The Trinity keeps us balanced.
6.examples:
Then: John's vision of heaven shows God on the throne, the Lamb who was slain, and the seven spirits of God before the throne, which many take to mean the Holy Spirit (Rev 4-5). All heaven worships. The Trinity is the centre of heaven's worship.

Now: A Christian begins ending each day with the words of 2 Corinthians 13:14 as a prayer for her family. She thanks the Father for his love, the Son for his grace and the Spirit for his fellowship. This simple habit changes how she thinks about God.

A simple test: Which person of the Trinity do you think about least? How could you grow in knowing him?

verseByVerse.quote: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Aim for restoration, comfort one another, agree with one another, live in peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul's final words to a troubled church call them to restoration, comfort, agreement and peace. The God of love and peace will be with them. Then he blesses them with the grace of Christ, the love of God and the fellowship of the Spirit. The Trinity is the source of the church's life together.

verseByVerse.quote: For this reason I bow my knees before the Father, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named, that according to the riches of his glory he may grant you to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in your inner being, so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith—that you, being rooted and grounded in love, may have strength to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul prays to the Father, asking that believers be strengthened by the Spirit so that Christ may dwell in their hearts by faith. He longs for them to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge and to be filled with all the fullness of God. Christian prayer is shaped by the Trinity.

verseByVerse.quote: Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord; and there are varieties of activities, but it is the same God who empowers them all in everyone. To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; varieties of service, but the same Lord; varieties of activities, but the same God who empowers them all. The church's diversity and unity reflect the Trinity. Each member is given a manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.

verseByVerse.quote: Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and how inscrutable his ways! "For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counselor?" "Or who has given a gift to him that he might be repaid?" For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be glory forever. Amen. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: After eleven chapters of deep theology, Paul bursts into praise. God's riches, wisdom and knowledge are unsearchable. No one has given him counsel. From him, through him and to him are all things. Studying the Trinity should end where Paul ends: in worship.

6.reflection:
How does knowing God as Father, Son and Spirit shape your prayers?

What does it mean that God has always been a fellowship of love?

How should the unity of the Trinity shape the unity of your church?

Pray 2 Corinthians 13:14 for someone this week.
